re_line: Quad leaders convene in Manila as Trump heads to Xi-Putin summit · PNG's Marape tells Xi Taiwan office closure 'wasn't easy' · Solomons opposition accuses Canberra of 'chequebook diplomacy' · RBA minutes show cash rate lifted to 4.85% · Cyclone Xavier hits Category 4 over Cook Islands
morning_memo: Albanese gets under an hour with Trump in Manila before Trump sits down with Xi Jinping and Putin, as the Quad holds its first in-person leaders' summit in more than two years.
Papua New Guinea's Marape told Xi that shutting Taiwan's representative office in Port Moresby 'wasn't easy,' confirming Taiwan no longer operates in the country.
Cyclone Xavier strengthened to Category 4 over the Northern Cook Islands, prompting Emergency Management Cook Islands to urge communities across five island groups to remain sheltered.

top_stories.headline: Albanese has under an hour to sway Trump before Xi-Putin summit
top_stories.body: **Anthony Albanese** has under an hour with **Donald Trump** in Manila before Trump sits down with **Xi Jinping** and **Vladimir Putin**, SMH reported. Trump landed waving the US and Philippines flags as a band played YMCA. The two join Quad counterparts tonight for the first in-person Quad leaders' summit in *more than two years*.
top_stories.src_line: per SMH Federal Politics (Natassia Chrysanthos): "Albanese has less than an hour to sway Trump before Xi and Putin summit" · also NYT, SMH World

top_stories.headline: PNG's Marape tells Xi closing Taiwan office 'wasn't easy'
top_stories.body: Papua New Guinea Prime Minister **James Marape** told **Xi Jinping** that closing a Taiwan representative office in Port Moresby 'wasn't easy,' Reuters reported, confirming Taiwan no longer operates in the country. The remarks came as Marape met the Chinese president during Xi's Asia travel this week.
top_stories.src_line: per Reuters: "Papua New Guinea prime minister tells Xi it 'wasn't easy' to close Taiwan office"

top_stories.headline: Solomons opposition leader accuses Australia of 'chequebook diplomacy'
top_stories.body: Solomon Islands' opposition leader accused Australia of practicing 'chequebook diplomacy' in the Pacific nation, ABC Pacific reported. The claim lands as Canberra's aid and budget-support programs across the Solomons face fresh domestic scrutiny.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC Pacific: "Solomon Islands opposition leader accuses Australia of 'chequebook diplomacy'"

overnight_items.headline: Albanese presses Laos PM over methanol poisoning deaths
overnight_items.body_text: Albanese raised the 2024 methanol poisoning deaths of two young Australian backpackers with Laos's prime minister, who said his government would review the criminal trials and any new evidence. The exchange came on the sidelines of Albanese's Southeast Asia diplomatic swing through Manila.

overnight_items.headline: Trump's advisers divided over China ahead of Xi summit
overnight_items.body_text: Divisions within the Trump administration over China policy have surfaced ahead of his meeting with Xi Jinping, The Australian reported, as Washington weighs chip export controls against efforts to stabilise relations. The split bears on how allies including Australia read US resolve heading into the Quad summit.

overnight_items.headline: Australia signs US-led AI agreement ahead of Trump meeting
overnight_items.body_text: Australia has joined a US-led agreement to secure technology and critical-minerals supply chains underpinning the AI boom, ABC reported, timed just before Albanese's meeting with Trump in Manila. The announcement follows days of market turmoil tied to Nvidia's leadership crisis and tightening US export controls on China.

overnight_items.headline: Ascent to support US-based RAAF Super Hornet, Growler fleets
overnight_items.body_text: Ascent has been contracted to provide sustainment support for Royal Australian Air Force Super Hornet and Growler aircraft based in the United States, Australian Defence Magazine reported. The arrangement extends Australia's reliance on US-based maintenance infrastructure for its strike and electronic-warfare fleets.

overnight_items.headline: Australian media giants launch campaign against AI training
overnight_items.body_text: Nine Entertainment, News Corp, Seven, Guardian Australia, Foxtel and Free TV Australia will launch a campaign, Not AI's To Take, demanding AI platforms secure permission and pay creators before training on Australian content, SMH reported. The campaign urges Australians to lobby local MPs starting Wednesday.

overnight_items.headline: Rio Tinto signs 50MW power deal for New Zealand smelter restart
overnight_items.body_text: Rio Tinto signed a *50MW* electricity contract to support the restart of Line 4 at its New Zealand aluminium operation, according to a company announcement carried by the Financial Times. The deal underpins a partial capacity restoration after the line's earlier curtailment.

aukus_watch.headline: ASPI: Australian ocean research aids China's submarine warfare
aukus_watch.body_text: Australia and its AUKUS partners are cooperating in oceanographic research with China that helps Beijing develop the submarine-detection capabilities AUKUS is designed to counter, ASPI Strategist reported. One Chinese military university is already converting international ocean-observation data for military use, the piece said.

aukus_watch.headline: Safety concerns raised after US submarine hits sea floor
aukus_watch.body_text: Australian Defence Magazine reported safety concerns for Australian sailors following an incident in which a US submarine struck the sea floor. The episode raises fresh questions about operational safety as US and UK boats rotate through Australian waters under AUKUS Pillar 1.

pacific_wire.headline: Ireland secures Pacific Islands Forum partnership status
pacific_wire.body_text: Ireland has been admitted as a Sectoral Partner of the Pacific Islands Forum, Irish Foreign Minister **Helen McEntee** said, aiming to deepen Dublin's engagement with Pacific states on climate change, ocean governance and sustainable development.

pacific_wire.headline: Kiribati minister: climate finance procedures must not delay funds
pacific_wire.body_text: Kiribati's climate minister told ABC Pacific at COP31 that procedural hurdles must not delay vulnerable states' access to climate finance, pressing larger emitters for faster disbursement mechanisms.

pacific_wire.headline: PNG's proposed three-child policy splits health experts
pacific_wire.body_text: Prime Minister **James Marape** announced plans for a national family-planning policy encouraging families to limit births to three children, aiming to ease pressure on a population of *10.18 million*, nearly half of whom are children, RNZ Pacific reported. A University of PNG professor welcomed the move but said it should have come 'a generation ago.'

pacific_wire.headline: Cyclone Xavier intensifies to Category 4 over Northern Cook Islands
pacific_wire.body_text: Severe Tropical Cyclone Xavier strengthened to Category 4 with winds reaching *165kph* and gusts to 240kph, the Cook Islands Meteorological Service said. Emergency Management Cook Islands urged communities in Manihiki, Rakahanga, Pukapuka, Nassau and Suwarrow to remain in shelter as conditions worsen into Tuesday.

pacific_wire.headline: Report urges protection for PNG environmental rights defenders
pacific_wire.body_text: A new report calls for stronger protection of environmental human rights advocates in Papua New Guinea, ABC Pacific reported, amid growing pressure on activists opposing extractive projects.

pacific_wire.headline: Tuvalu turns nappy waste into opportunity
pacific_wire.body_text: A Tuvalu initiative is converting disposable nappy waste into a resource opportunity, Islands Business reported, part of a broader push against plastic pollution in a region generating outsized waste relative to its size.

new_zealand.stand_in: No significant New Zealand developments in the past 24 hours.

canberra_politics.headline: Independent MPs blast Labor's late changes to election funding laws
canberra_politics.body_text: Crossbenchers say last-minute government amendments to incoming federal electoral laws would let an *uncapped amount of money* flow to major parties through investment funds, Guardian Australia reported. The government introduced the changes on Tuesday, describing them as 'technical,' weeks before the new laws take effect.

canberra_politics.headline: Greens to poll members on Ukraine military aid after backlash
canberra_politics.body_text: The Greens will ask members to vote on the party's stance on Australian military aid to Ukraine, SMH reported, after the position attracted fierce criticism. The review follows sustained condemnation of the party's earlier opposition to supporting Kyiv militarily.

canberra_politics.headline: Canberra wanted 1,000 digital trainees, agencies hired 73
canberra_politics.body_text: Australian government agencies hired just *73* digital trainees against a target of one thousand, Politico reported, exposing a gap in the public service's push to build in-house technology capability.

canberra_politics.headline: Watchdog orders new search for Afghanistan killing documents
canberra_politics.body_text: Australia's transparency watchdog has ordered the Department of Defence to conduct a new search for documents related to alleged Afghanistan killings, Politico reported, reopening a long-running freedom-of-information dispute.

canberra_politics.headline: MP declared data centre shares before calling for moratorium
canberra_politics.body_text: An MP declared shares in a data centre developer shortly before calling for a moratorium on new developments, ABC reported, raising questions about parliamentary conflict-of-interest disclosure.

canberra_politics.headline: Chalmers flags 'Goldilocks' balance for budget update
canberra_politics.body_text: Treasurer **Jim Chalmers** said next month's budget update would balance spending cuts against protecting the broader economy, SMH reported, as he seeks to calm inflation pressure without choking growth.

business_economy.headline: RBA minutes show dissenters feared 'sharper downturn'
business_economy.body_text: Three RBA board members dissented from November's decision to lift the cash rate to *4.85 per cent*, warning of a sharper downturn, AFR reported from the minutes. The majority judged persistent inflation pressure outweighed the growth and unemployment risks the dissenters raised.

business_economy.headline: China flexes muscle in iron ore, squeezing Australian miners
business_economy.body_text: Beijing is tightening its grip on iron ore purchasing arrangements in ways that squeeze Australia and its miners, WSJ reported, as China leverages its buying power over the commodity that underpins much of Australia's export revenue.

business_economy.headline: Australia opens anti-dumping probe into Chinese timber
business_economy.body_text: Australia will investigate China over alleged timber dumping, Bloomberg reported, the latest in a series of anti-dumping actions targeting Chinese exports to the Australian market.

business_economy.headline: New Zealand dollar slumps to a six-year low
business_economy.body_text: The New Zealand dollar fell to its weakest level in six years, WSJ reported. The currency traded at *0.5499* against the US dollar, down 1.93 percent, as traders price in a widening rate differential with other major economies.

business_economy.headline: NZ banks earn wider margins on loans than Australian peers
business_economy.body_text: New Zealand banks make more money on their loans than Australian counterparts, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand said in its latest financial stability report, per RNZ, with net interest margins generally higher in New Zealand over the past decade. The central bank said home-loan borrowing costs are set to rise.

calendar_watch.event: Quad Leaders Summit convenes in Manila
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: First in-person Quad summit in more than two years, marking Trump's debut at the forum Biden elevated to annual status.

calendar_watch.event: Cyclone Xavier threatens Northern Cook Islands
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Category 4 storm prompts high alert across five island groups as conditions worsen into Tuesday.
Treasurer Chalmers has flagged a balance between spending cuts and protecting household relief amid inflation pressure.
First electoral test for Liberal leader Jess Wilson and Labor's Ben Carroll against a projected net debt of $173.5 billion.

key_stat.label: RBA cash rate after November rate rise
key_stat.context: Three RBA board members dissented over fears of a sharper downturn, AFR reported from the minutes, but the majority still voted to lift rates.

also_today.headline: ASPI: Philippines treaty fills gap in Australia's China strategy
also_today.body_text: The new Defence Cooperation Arrangement signed in Manila recognises that defending Australia's maritime trade requires a network of regional partners, ASPI Strategist argued. The piece frames the Philippines relationship as critical to Australia's defence posture against China.

also_today.headline: ASPI backs Albanese on keeping religious motivation in terror law
also_today.body_text: Albanese is right to resist a proposal to strip religious motivation from terrorism legislation, ASPI Strategist argued, backing the government's position over the independent national security legislation monitor's recommendation.

also_today.headline: Devpolicy: Australian aid has gone backwards on evidence
also_today.body_text: A new paper on aid effectiveness echoes Devpolicy's founding arguments, the blog said, asking why Australian aid has regressed on using evidence even as accountability paperwork keeps growing.

also_today.headline: Lowy: APEC delivers, just not what Canberra hoped for
also_today.body_text: Xi, Trump and Putin will meet in Shenzhen while the forum's Australian architects watch from the sidelines, the Lowy Interpreter wrote, arguing APEC's original Australian-driven vision has been overtaken by great-power theatre.

also_today.headline: Lowy podcast: India, Australia and Japan look 'beyond the Quad'
also_today.body_text: A Lowy Institute podcast examines how India, Australia and Japan are deepening ties beyond the Quad framework, as the grouping's leaders meet in Manila for their first in-person summit in more than two years.
